# Moodle CLI 0.13.0

This release adds opt-in Okta sign-in for the CLI and the private MCP Worker, fixes sign-in, updates and downloads on Windows, and reworks the home screen and help.

## Highlights

- **Okta sign-in for the CLI, opt-in.** `moodle auth login --okta` signs in through the okta-auth CLI and renews through it later.
- **The MCP Worker signs in by itself.** `moodle mcp deploy --okta` stores your Okta username, password and TOTP secret as Worker secrets, so an expired session no longer waits for you.
- **Careful with your account.** Nothing retries a rejected password or one-time code, and consent is confirmed per site.
- **Windows works end to end.** `moodle auth login` finds Chrome again, `moodle update` and MCP deploys run, and downloaded file names are safe on NTFS.
- **A calmer home screen.** One loading spinner instead of a flicker per request, a cleaner layout, and an `Update` row when a new version is out.
- **Help ordered by what saves you time.** Downloads and submitting come first, then the agent skill, then reading.

## Okta sign-in for the CLI

```bash
npm install -g okta-auth-cli
okta-auth setup
moodle auth login --okta
```

For a Moodle site behind Okta, `moodle auth login --okta` signs in through the okta-auth CLI and keeps using it when the session needs renewing. It runs `okta-auth` from npm, or `okta` from the Python package (`uv tool install okta-auth-cli`), which wins when both are installed. If it cannot sign in, it stops with okta's reason instead of opening the browser. Turn it off again with `moodle auth login --no-okta`.

The first `--okta` for a site asks you to confirm, because okta sends your Okta password and one-time code to whichever identity provider that site redirects to. The choice is saved for that site's address in your own `~/.config/moodle-cli/config.yaml` only, so a project's `config.yaml` cannot turn it on.

Without `--okta`, an installed okta-auth CLI is only read: a session it already saved for the site is reused, and it never signs in. Background renewal never signs in. Once Okta rejects the password, moodle-cli stops signing in through it until you fix the credentials and run `moodle auth login --okta` again, because repeated attempts can lock the account. Sites that do not use Okta see no change.

## The MCP Worker signs in through Okta

```bash
moodle mcp deploy --okta
```

With okta-auth-cli 0.3.0 or later set up, `--okta` runs its `export` and adds `OKTA_USERNAME`, `OKTA_PASSWORD` and `OKTA_TOTP_SECRET` to the same private upload as the Worker's own credentials. When the Moodle session is missing or expired, the Worker then signs in to Moodle through Okta itself, after the Moodle mobile token if it has one.

Your university identity then becomes only as safe as your Cloudflare account. Anyone who controls that account can read or replace the Worker and sign in as you, MFA included. Only use `--okta` if you accept that.

The Worker never retries a rejected password or one-time code, an MFA factor other than TOTP, or a sign-in that lands on a different Moodle account. It stops until you change one of the three secrets. Network and Okta outages back off and stop after five failures in a row. Okta's device token and session are kept encrypted between runs, so most renewals skip the password entirely.

`moodle mcp status` says the Worker signs in again through Okta by itself. The Worker's `/readyz` adds an `okta:sign-in` check, which reads `OKTA_READY` or says why the Worker stopped.

Later deploys keep the secrets. To remove them, run `npx wrangler secret delete OKTA_USERNAME --name WORKER_NAME`, and the same for `OKTA_PASSWORD` and `OKTA_TOTP_SECRET`. To add them to an existing Worker by hand, pipe them straight into Wrangler:

```bash
okta-auth export --dangerously-print-password-and-totp-secret | npx wrangler secret bulk --name WORKER_NAME
```

## Windows

The full test suite now runs on Windows in CI, and it found these:

- `moodle auth login` reported that no Chromium browser was installed when Windows spelled `ProgramFiles` in mixed case. Thanks to @scarlyhalon for the report and the fix (#80, #81).
- `moodle update` and the first MCP deploy failed with `EINVAL`, because Node refuses to start `npm.cmd` and `wrangler.cmd` without a shell. They now run through `cmd.exe`.
- A download named like `Week 1: Intro.pdf` was written into an NTFS alternate data stream of a file called `Week 1`, where nobody would look. Characters Windows cannot store are now dropped from file names, and extensions in any script are kept.
- Paths in output now use the platform separator.

## Home screen

A bare `moodle` shows one spinner while it loads, however many requests it makes, and clears it before anything is printed. The screen leads with your name, date, time zone and site, lists what is due in a table, and lines up unread messages, units and current weeks under one column of labels.

When a newer version is out, the home screen shows an `Update` row every time. Other commands mention it after their output, at most once a day, instead of before it where it scrolled away.

## Help

`moodle --help` groups commands by how much time they save over the web page: Get work done (`sync`, `download`, `submit`, `due`, `grades`), Use with an agent (`skills`, `mcp`), Browse and read, Set up, and Older views (`overview`, `todo`, `alerts`, `user`). `attempt` and `update` no longer fall into a stray group.
